purpose:
1                   
Decision

1.1            
Following consideration of the
officer report (exempt from publication under Schedule 12A of the
Local Government Act 1972), the Leader and Deputy Leader have
agreed the following:

1.2            
That the property at 33a High
Street, Bushey be disposed of for a revised purchase price being
the best consideration reasonably obtainable following the
withdrawal of the previously-approved purchaser.

1.3            
That the disposal shall proceed by
placing the original prospective purchaser and the second-highest
bidder into a contracts race at the same purchase price to
determine the final purchaser in a fair and transparent
manner.

1.4            
That the Head of Asset Management,
in consultation with Legal Services, is authorised to take all
necessary steps to implement this decision, including the
completion of the relevant legal documentation.

 

2                   
Reasons for the
Decision

2.1            
The previously approved purchaser
withdrew after being unable to secure finance, requiring a revised
decision.

2.2            
The revised figure reflects the
next best consideration reasonably obtainable.

2.3            
Officer delegated authority does
not extend to a disposal at a lower price than that approved by
Cabinet, and therefore Executive approval was required.

2.4            
The agreed disposal route provides
a fair, transparent and expedient mechanism to achieve an early
exchange of contracts.

 

3                   
Alternative
Options Considered

 

3.1           
Retaining the
asset
-
Rejected due
to
ongoing
holding costs,
deterioration risk, and lack of viable rental prospects.

3.2            
Re-marketing
the property
- Rejected
due to
likely delays,
costs, and the risk of securing a lower
offer in current market conditions.

 

4                   

Call-In

4.1           
This
decision is subject
to Call-In under the Council's Overview and Scrutiny Procedure
Rules.

4.2            
It
will
come
into
force
after
the
expiry
of
five
clear
working
days
from
the
date
of
publication
unless
called
in.

purpose:
Hertsmere’s current Financial
Strategy was last approved by the full Council in July 2018
covering the period 2018/19 to 2021/22 (C/18/27). This strategy was
based on the then current economic conditions, government funding
and other pressures and influences that were likely to impact on
the Council’s finances at that time.

A revised draft Financial Strategy
was presented to the Cabinet in September 2025 for consideration
and the Cabinet recommended the draft Financial Strategy to the
Policy Review Committee for their review and comment.

The draft Financial Strategy was
presented to the Policy Review Committee at their meeting on 4
November 2025. The Committee raised a number of questions in
relation to homelessness, savings, reserves and contingency,
Council Tax, Hertsmere Developments Limited and the Fair Funding
Review. These were responded to by the Assistant Director –
Finance and are recorded in the draft printed minutes.

Subsequent to the Financial
Strategy being presented to the Policy Committee, the outcome of
the Fair Funding Review and the resulting multi-year provisional
finance settlement covering the spending review period 2025/26 to
2028/29 was announced on 17 December 2025.

The Fair Funding Review and
multi-year settlement are discussed in the Revenue Budget report
earlier on this agenda and the Financial Strategy has now been
further updated to reflect the latest funding position.
The Cabinet
considered the updated Financial Strategy 2026 on the 14 January
2026 to consider recommendation to the Full Council for
adoption. 
An update will be given at the meeting if
appropriate.

purpose:
Local housing authorities are
required by law (Part 6 of the Housing Act 1996 as amended) to have
a Housing Allocations Policy which sets out how the council will
allocate social housing within the borough.

The current Housing Allocations
Policy was implemented in November 2019 with minor revisions made
under a Portfolio Holder Decision in August 2022.

The revised Housing Allocations
Policy makes some proposed changes in regards to the eligibility
criteria (Section 5) which attempt to achieve a more balanced
response to addressing updated housing needs amidst a significant
shortage in social housing.
On
10th July, new
local connection exemptions for care leavers under the age of 25
and victims of domestic abuse who subsequently had to leave their
home due to the abuse came into force nationally. The Draft Policy
has been amended to reflect these changes.
